title: HATCH gradient DXF field-grammar fast slice
mode: source-backed local implementation and generated fast verification
scope: Implement HATCH gradient group-presence and companion-field validation for ASCII and Binary DXF
Apply equivalent active-gradient writer preflight checks
Preserve retained-text budget replacement behavior for repeated group 470

sources.title: Autodesk HATCH DXF reference
sources.finding: When group 450 is present, the gradient control block requires groups 451, 452, 453, 460, 461, 462, and 470; group 453 is zero for a solid fill and two for a gradient fill. The group 451 and 463 role values are reserved/defined by the documented block. The table does not define duplicate-group handling.

sources.title: Autodesk Group Code Value Types Reference
sources.finding: Codes 430-439 are strings, 450-459 are 32-bit integers, 460-469 are doubles, and 470-479 are strings; group 431 cannot be emitted as a typed integer based on generic group-code classification.

observations: The parser now tracks required gradient-field presence, detects orphan companion groups, and checks the complete companion block at entity validation.
Active gradient validation requires mode 1, reserved field zero, single-color mode 0/1, two stops at positions 0 and 1, finite scalar values, and tint in [0,1] only for single-color mode.
Solid mode requires a zero stop count with no stop records but ignores other present companion values.

Group 470 uses retained-string replacement and remains last-value-wins because the Autodesk grammar reviewed does not specify duplicate policy; this preserves the pre-existing retained-budget contract.
The generated ASCII/Binary selector covers complete positive blocks, malformed presence/duplicates/count/order, tint boundaries, and repeated group-470 replacement.

validation.compatibility: PASS: lc3_compat_check after the public-header parser-state addition

remaining: HATCH gradient 431 mapping remains unresolved and is not emitted as an integer.
HATCH-specific semantic meaning of gradient name/book groups 432/433 remains unresolved.
Cross-consumer gradient rendering and full HATCH interoperability remain unqualified.
